newsitem.title: UKRAINE: WET WEATHER POSES THREAT TO UKRAINE GRAIN-AG MIN.
newsitem.headline: WET WEATHER POSES THREAT TO UKRAINE GRAIN-AG MIN.

text.p: Heavy, constant rain is posing a threat to Ukraine's grain harvest which was previously forecast at 37-38 million tonnes this year, newly-appointed Agriculture Minister Yuri Karasyk said on Thursday.
"I have worked in the agrarian sector for 35 years and I have never seen such weather," Karasyk told a news conference.

"The grain is wet. All of our dryers are working full-time so we can dry the grain. Our job this year is not just to bring the harvest in but to bring the grain up to a good condition and to save it," Karasyk said.

Weather forecasts are calling for more rain in the next few days. A precipitation-filled July pushed harvesting back about two weeks later than average, and there was only a brief sunny break for several days at the end of last month.
Karasyk said it would be possible to more accurately forecast grain output in 10 to 12 days.
"We have gathered 60 percent of the harvest. We have 17 million tonnes," he said.

Last year's harvest was 25.4 million tonnes and a drought at the start of the growing season was blamed for the poor figure in a country which regularly produced harvests of 50 million tonnes during Soviet times.
But Karasyk said Ukraine, which has poor facilities for drying and storing grain properly, would probably not need to import grain this year.
"I doubt we will need to buy grain from abroad," he said.
He added Ukraine would definitely export but said it was too early to tell how much.
Karasyk's predecessor Mykhailo Zubets, who was sacked in July, in April forecast grain exports at 10 million tonnes.
"We are expecting a very nice corn harvest," Karasyk added. Last year Ukraine produced 1.8 million tonnes of maize, against 2.2 million tonnes in 1995.
